labels.label: bzprop:c3s6p4_deux_points_extremaux
labels.notes: deux_points_extremaux (PointsExtremaux.lean:194) carries exactly the printed hypotheses: 0 < n (the printed n >= 1) and IsCorpsConvexeS n W (Projective/Convex.lean:542, Ch. 1 Def. 11: strict convex, compact, nonempty interior). It concludes the existence of f, g with IsFacetteK W f, IsFacetteK W g (the strict Chapter3/FacettesSphere Def. 4 classes, FacettesSphere.lean:343, nonempty by construction), f != g, f = {a}, g = {b}. That is Lean = paper: no added hypothesis and no narrowing. Krein-Milman comes from Mathlib (IsCompact.extremePoints_nonempty, closure_convexHull_extremePoints) applied to the compact convex section {v in F(W) | l v = 1}; it is not assumed. The step from 'at least one' to 'at least two' extreme points is proved: if there were only one, {mk p} would be clopen in the connected S(n) (connectedSpace_S), contradicting neg_ne_self. The remark 'facette reduced to a point = extreme point' is Sphere.facetteK_eq_singleton_iff_mem_extremePoints, proved in both directions over any real vector space, for a convex part k and l > 0 on F(k). deux_points_extremaux_iff proves the conclusion for all convex bodies of S(n) iff 0 < n; the n = 0 direction uses isCorpsConvexeS_singleton_S0 (strict Hilbert.lean:1502). The instance is real: isCorpsConvexeS_simplexS is proved (convexity of F, compactness, open positive-orthant interior), the vertices are extreme points of the standard simplex section, vertex_injective holds, and triangle_three_facettes gives three pairwise distinct one-point facettes of the closed triangle of S(2). The bold mark is honest. The checklist and SCOPE are present and true (the hyperplane-section chart instead of instAddTorsorHemi is disclosed and is the same chart). The three REPORT findings are accurate: (1) the printed n >= 1 is needed and is printed, so this is not a defect; (2) the remark holds in both directions; (3) the printed proof leaves the existence of a second extreme point implicit, and this is a real but small gap that the Lean closes.

build.notes: lake env lean scaffold/BenzecriScaffold/Chapter3/PointsExtremaux.lean exited 0 with no output. grep -c sorry gives 1, and the one match is the docstring text 'no `sorry`' (l.69), not a proof hole. A one-shot probe (deleted afterwards) printed axioms for deux_points_extremaux, deux_points_extremaux_iff, not_two_singleton_facettes_S0, Sphere.facetteK_eq_singleton_iff_mem_extremePoints and TriangleInstance.triangle_three_facettes: each gives [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. Scope: the closer's paths are PointsExtremaux.lean, the PointsExtremaux import line in BenzecriScaffold.lean and the campaign directory. The second new import line (Chapter3.DualiteInterieur) belongs to the concurrent T-bz-c3-dualite-interieur closer. The other modified files in git status (restatements, roadmaps) were already modified at session start and belong to other loops. REPORT's 'one import line appended' is true of this target.

findings.what: The helper not_two_singleton_facettes_S0 is listed among the label's declarations. tools/restate.py NEG_PART (^not_) would therefore make bzprop:c3s6p4_deux_points_extremaux a STRONG restatement candidate, i.e. a refutation of the printed statement. It refutes nothing printed: it is the n = 0 case, which the printed bound n >= 1 already excludes. Leaving the name as is would put a spurious entry in the restate register, which then has to be dismissed by hand.
findings.fix: Rename it to a positive name without a not_ component, e.g. S0_two_singleton_facettes_false or S0_singleton_facettes_eq (stating that a convex body of S(0) has at most one one-point facette), and update the docstring and REPORT decls. Or drop it from the label's decls and keep only deux_points_extremaux_iff, which carries the same content under a neutral name.
